svg.text: TIDAL STREAM ATLAS · THE WESTERN SOLENT AND HURST NARROWS
tidal streams · tenths of a knot at neaps and at springs
HW DOVER -1 h
HOW TO READ AN ARROW
weak at springs
moderate at springs
strong at springs
0.8 knots at neaps (coefficient 45)
1.5 knots at springs (coefficient 95)
the arrow points WHERE THE WATER GOES, in degrees true
«HOW TO USE IT»
1 · on the almanac's tide pages, the day's HW DOVER, in UTC. 2 · the difference between the time you want and that high water, rounded to the hour: that is the page.
3 · the THREE ARROWS around the place; each gives a direction and, between its two figures, the day's knots. 4 · share them in inverse proportion to distance:
the nearest weighs most. Drawn all three from the same point and the difference split, that is the stream. The checker reads this page the same way.
«HOW TO INTERPOLATE BETWEEN NEAPS AND SPRINGS»
With the COEFFICIENT of the tide pages whose Brest time, printed under it, is nearest yours: knots = neaps + (springs − neaps) × (coefficient − 45) / 50.
Example: arrow 08,15 and coefficient 70 → 0.8 + (1.5 − 0.8) × 25/50 = 1.15, so 1.2 knots. Coefficient 112 → 0.8 + 0.7 × 1.34 = 1.7 knots.
Without a coefficient, the day's RANGE at Dover will do: mean neap range 3.12 m, mean spring range 6.05 m; place the day's range between the two in the same proportion.
«WHAT THIS PAGE DOES NOT SAY»
Between two arrows the stream is not the mean of the two: measured on THIS sheet, the difference exceeds 0.4 knots in 5 % of cases and reaches 0.9 at worst.
The arrows are samples, not a field. Where the Shom grid does not reach there is no arrow, and that includes harbour mouths and, here, the rivers, and Southampton Water above Hythe.
Each arrow IS on a real node of the Shom grid and says what the atlas says there: no cell average, no maximum moved from its place. In a race the node falls on the axis.
The thirteen pages run on HW DOVER; the Shom grids run on their own port's, and the offset —measured over the high waters of 2024— is already applied:
Cherbourg HW -196 min, Dover HW +0 min. It is the only step between this sheet and the data.
○ The 22 arrows with a circle are not from the Shom, whose grid does not reach there: they are the TIDAL stream of Copernicus's AMM15 model,
taken from a year of its hourly currents and CALIBRATED against the Shom offshore (M2 x 0.90 and +5.5 degrees; M4 x 0.74). In shallow water the error may be larger.
DASHED circle (17): a cell by the shore that AMM15 only reads at the neighbouring node, less than 1.5 km away; the arrow is at that node and says what it says there.
Generated using E.U. Copernicus Marine Service Information; https://doi.org/10.48670/moi-00054
Shom, 2026. Atlas de courants de maree 2D au format netcdf, https://dx.doi.org/10.17183/ATLASCOURANTS2D_NETCDF · Licence Ouverte 2.0.
